Keep the soft, round, bright 3D render look of the pictures, not a 2D drawing and no outlines. The children keep their chibi proportions: a big head and a small body. Hands are small, chubby child hands with five clear short fingers (four fingers and one thumb) when open, never fists unless stated, and a hanging hand shows relaxed, separate short fingers. Each eye ends in a smooth, rounded corner; Nan alone keeps one short, thick, curved eyelash flick at each outer eye corner. Clean eye corners, no streak on the forehead, no marks on the face. linePrompt: Picture 1 is a 3D-rendered children's book picture. Convert picture 1 to line art for a student book: thick, even black lines (about three times a normal outline), simple closed shapes that a 5-year-old can color, on pure white. No blush circles, no eyelash ticks, no hair strands, no shading, no gray, no texture lines, no text. Keep every shape in the same place and the same size. Draw each eye as a closed outline with a big solid black pupil (a filled black circle) inside it. Draw the mouth exactly as in picture 1: an open mouth stays an open mouth drawn as a closed outline, and a closed smile stays one curve. Draw each hand as a closed outline with each finger as a separate rounded shape. Each head of hair is one closed shape. The ear is one closed outline with at most one inner curve. No lines on the clothes other than the outline, the collar, and the star. Simplify the background: draw only a few large, simple, closed shapes (the floor line, the wall line, two or three big closed beam shapes, the window as one closed square, each easel as one closed frame, the table as one closed shape, the toy kitchen and the shelf as large closed box shapes). No wood grain lines, no floor plank lines, no plaster texture, no hatching, no tick marks, no small details on the shelf. Every outline is one closed line that never runs into a background line; no loose line ends anywhere. Every line inside an object ends on another line. Use few background shapes. Nan keeps her painted eyelash mark in the line art: at the outer corner of each visible eye, draw ONE short thick solid stroke (as thick as the outline) that touches the eye outline. The eyelash stroke is the only mark beside each eye. Each hair bun is one closed circle with its red band as one closed strip. Pip: the whole puppy is one closed outline with no fur strands; the ears, the collar, and the round tag are separate closed shapes; each eye is one closed outline with a big solid black pupil. The paint spots on Pip are a few closed round blob shapes.
